findings.title: G32 accepts a terminal challenge that skipped mandatory arm diversity
findings.why_it_matters: The terminal trust gate can certify HALT_SUCCESS without any simplicity or domain-modeling attack.
findings.what_is_wrong: halt-verifier.md requires a simplicity/domain_modeling challenge arm, but check_g32_halt_success_challenge validates only that attempts is non-empty; the positive held fixture uses only data_flow.
findings.leverage_impact: The existing G32 Interface can enforce the documented challenge contract for every terminal run.
findings.locality_impact: The rule and fixture currently disagree with the validator that owns terminal promotion.
findings.metric_signal: One positive terminal fixture omits the mandatory non-correctness arm.
findings.why_weakens_submission: A reachable terminal path can bypass a required dimension of independent scrutiny, leaving the success claim structurally under-validated.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extend G32 to validate attempt shape and require one new_finding attempt targeting simplicity or domain_modeling; add that arm to the valid fixture and a failing no-diversity fixture.

simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Do not extract the two-site replication similarity without current drift or duplicated runtime authority.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: No fix pending; full suite is the terminal oracle.
